notes: The SET/audit question explicitly scopes idempotence to the requested register effect; this avoids conflating incidental delivery logs with that effect.
The historical-result question states exact stored-result replay, rather than assuming all real APIs return a byte-identical or current-state reply.
Atomicity, identity namespace, mismatch refusal and retention are expressly declared teaching contracts; the answers do not claim every HTTP service implements them.
The concurrency trace expressly makes increments atomic and sequentially applied after both initial reads, excluding a lost-update interpretation.
The late SET trace deliberately separates repeat idempotence from protection against intervening writes.
The final at-most-once question includes non-delivery explicitly, so zero effects is compatible with the safety property.
